items.prompt: White to move. Black has just taken the pawn on c4. Find a good move. Two of the good moves are queen moves that attack that pawn.

claims.statement: c4 holds the black pawn.
No white piece attacks c4 yet.
After Qc2 the queen attacks c4.
After Qa4 the queen attacks c4.
At depth 16 Qc2, Qa4 and Ne5 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move.

hints: Which white piece stands on d1, and which squares on the c-file or the fourth rank can it reach?
The queen can attack the pawn from the second rank or from the fourth rank.
Qc2 and Qa4 both attack c4 (Ne5 is also close to the best).
items.explain: No white piece attacks the pawn on c4 yet. Qc2 and Qa4 both attack it, and at depth 16 both are within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move, as is Ne5. Attacking the pawn with the queen is one sound idea here, not the only one.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's b-pawn has left b7, but White's knight on f3 stands on the bishop's diagonal. Find the knight move that opens the diagonal.

claims.statement: b7 is empty.
Now the bishop on g2 does not attack a8.
After Ne5 the bishop on g2 attacks the rook on a8.
At depth 16 Ne5 is the engine's first choice.

hints: Count the squares between the bishop on g2 and the rook on a8. Which one holds a white piece?
The knight on f3 is the only piece in the way.
The knight goes to e5.
items.explain: With the pawn gone from b7, the only piece between the bishop on g2 and the rook on a8 is White's own knight on f3. After Ne5 the bishop attacks a8, and at depth 16 Ne5 is the engine's first choice. The idea needs the line to be empty apart from that knight; check it each time.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's bishop on g2 looks along the long diagonal and White's knight stands on f3 in front of it. Find the bishop move that puts a Black bishop on the same diagonal.

claims.statement: f3 holds the white knight.
After Bb7 the bishop attacks the knight on f3.
At depth 16 Bb7 is the engine's first choice.
At depth 16 c6 is at least 0.7 pawn worse than the best move.

hints: Which Black piece can reach the long diagonal in one move?
The bishop on c8 has a free square on b7.
The bishop goes to b7.
items.explain: Bb7 puts the bishop on the long diagonal: it attacks the knight on f3, which the bishop on g2 defends. At depth 16 it is the engine's first choice. A pawn move such as c6 may look like support for the pawn on b5, but the engine rates it at least 0.7 pawn lower.

feedback_by_move.c7c6: c6 supports the pawn on b5, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.7 pawn worse than Bb7. Supporting a pawn is not the same as finishing development.
